overview: Munich-headquartered maker of braking and safety-relevant sub-systems for rail and commercial vehicles, with a Rail Vehicle Systems segment and a Commercial Vehicle Systems division [37][38][41]. It reported €7.9bn revenue and 33,319 employees in 2023 [38], and its shares trade on the Frankfurt exchange (KBX, MDAX component) [38]. Sources describe it as listed since its 2018 IPO [37], and its 2018 DOJ filing called it privately owned at that time [10].

Operational_Resilience_Score.evidence: Nine-month 2024 EBIT margin was 11.8% with a €7.06bn order book, and 2025 was reported as another record year [3][35].

Financial_Health_Score.evidence: Equity ratio fell from 35.2% to 32.1% by September 2024, net debt was €1,308m at start of year, and nine-month free cash flow rose to €247.9m from €64.9m [2][3].

Quality_Risk_Score.evidence: Knorr-branded brake chambers were recalled under NHTSA 24V-559 and a Knorr radial brake caliper guide-pin defect was recalled in Proterra buses, though root-cause responsibility is not confirmed [11][12][13].

Compliance_Risk_Score.evidence: A 2018 DOJ Sherman Act no-poach settlement carries a Final Judgment with compliance inspection rights and antitrust compliance officer obligations, and the current status is not shown [6][9][10].

Credit_Rating_Score.evidence: S&P affirmed Knorr-Bremse at 'A-' with a stable outlook on November 26, 2024 [1].

Safety_Incident_Score.evidence: Products are safety-relevant and the recalls describe brake-related failure modes such as dragging brakes and guide-pin bolt breakage, but no Knorr-attributed incident is shown in the sources [11][12][14].

Sub_Tier_Visibility_Score.evidence: On-site supplier audits fell from 30 in 2022 to 10 in 2023, and a Knorr-branded chamber was made by a third party, ZF North America [12][21].

Geopolitical_Risk_Score.evidence: Russia sanctions hit the RVS segment (EBIT margin 13.3% in 2022), China-related pressure is cited, and about half of Asian sales are from China [28][30].

Governance_Risk_Score.evidence: The company has a published anti-corruption and compliance framework, but a DOJ no-poach settlement and a related private damages suit by employees add governance concerns [6][7][36].

ESG_Performance_Score.evidence: CDP climate rating reached Gold in 2023 (up from Silver), with human rights due diligence and sustainability audits reported [21][22].

Digital_Security_Score.evidence: A dedicated cybersecurity competence centre and a TCMS threat-detection product exist, but these are company-published and no incident is reported [23][25].

Market_Sentiment_Score.evidence: Analyst coverage describes a Q1 beat with a BUY rating and raised estimates, and market cap was about $17bn [2][37].

Media_Sentiment_Score.evidence: Coverage is mixed: one commentary calls it a 'Hidden Champion with a few issues', and the company publicly criticised Russia sanctions [27][30].

External_Intelligence_Score.evidence: External sources report a DOJ antitrust settlement, a private class suit, recurring brake recalls and sanctions exposure, but no current enforcement outcome is found [6][12][36].

red_flags.title: DOJ no-poach antitrust settlement with ongoing compliance obligations
red_flags.detail: On April 3, 2018 the DOJ settled Sherman Act Section 1 no-poach allegations with Knorr-Bremse and Wabtec, with a Final Judgment that includes compliance inspection rights. The term and current compliance status are not shown in the sources [6][9][10].

red_flags.title: Private employee antitrust damages suit over the same no-poach conspiracy
red_flags.detail: Employees of Knorr and Wabtec filed a proposed class damages suit over the alleged no-poach agreements. The filing is documented, but the ruling or settlement outcome is not shown [36].

red_flags.title: Brake chamber safety recall involving Knorr-branded components (NHTSA 24V-559)
red_flags.detail: NHTSA recall 24V-559 covers Knorr 20/22-57 brake chambers (part K038830N00) made by ZF North America. Nova Bus recalled about 2,090 units over a potential manufacturing defect, with root cause and remedy status not confirmed in the sources [12][13].

red_flags.title: Radial brake caliper guide-pin defect in Proterra buses (recall 18V-750)
red_flags.detail: A Knorr-supplied radial brake caliper guide pin with improper surface roughness could cause friction and potentially guide-pin bolt breakage. A free remedy was offered through a 2018 recall notice [11].

red_flags.title: Exposure to Russia sanctions and China-related margin pressure
red_flags.detail: Sanctions on Russia and the China situation reduced RVS segment EBIT margin to 13.3% in 2022. Current exposure figures and sanctions-compliance status are not confirmed [27][28].

strengths: Order book of €7.06bn at 30 Sep 2024 with a stable order intake [3]
CDP climate rating upgraded to Gold in 2023 [22]
On-site sustainability audits of suppliers and human rights due diligence process established [21]
Dedicated cybersecurity competence centre and TCMS threat-detection product [23][25]
recommendation: Approve with conditions, since the company is financially sound and the main risks are legal and quality-related rather than solvency-related. Ask for the current status and term of the 2018 DOJ Final Judgment and any compliance monitor reports, and for the outcome or status of the employee damages suit. Require root-cause analysis, remedy completion evidence and responsibility allocation (Knorr vs. ZF) for recalls 24V-559 and 18V-750, plus sanctions-compliance and China JV export-control confirmation for the current period. Also request sub-tier supplier audit coverage, since on-site audits fell from 30 in 2022 to 10 in 2023 [12][21][36].
